entries.title: Nehemiah 4:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 While the enemies scoff, Nehemiah prays and continues the work. 7 Understanding the wrath and secrets of the enemy, he sets a watch. 13 He arms the labourers; 19 and gives military precepts.

Sanballat. 2:10,19; Ezr 4:1-5; Ac 5:17 mocked. Ps 35:15,16; 44:13,14; Mt 27:29; Heb 11:36

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the army. Ezr 4:9,10 feeble. 1Sa 14:11,12; 17:43,44; Zec 12:8; 1Co 1:27 fortify themselves. Heb. leave to themselves. sacrifice. 12:27,43 revive. 10; Eze 37:3-13; Hab 3:2

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:4
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Hear. Ps 123:3,4 despised. Heb. despite. turn. 1Sa 17:26; Ps 79:12; Pr 3:34; Ho 12:14

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:5
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: cover not. Ps 59:5-13; 69:27; 109:14; Jer 18:23; 2Ti 4:14 their sin. Ps 51:1,9; Isa 43:25; 44:22 before the builders. Isa 36:11,12

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
and all the wall.That is, the whole circuit of the wall was completed unto half the intended height.

for the people.The original is very emphatic, {wyhee laiv l��m l��soth,} "for the people had a heart to work." Their heart was engaged in it, and they went about it cheerfully and vigorously.

had a mind. 6:15; 1Ch 29:3,14,17,18; 2Ch 29:36; Ps 110:3; 2Co 8:16,17 Php 2:13; Heb 13:21

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:8
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: all. Ps 2:1-3; 83:3-11; Isa 8:9,10; Ac 23:12,13 hinder it. Heb. make an error to it. Jer 20:10

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: The strength. Nu 13:31; 32:9; Ps 11:1,2; Hag 1:2 bearers. 2Ch 2:18; Eze 29:18

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:12
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: ten times. Ge 31:7,41; Nu 14:22; Job 19:3 From all places, etc. or, That from all places ye mustreturn to us. ye shall return. Houbigant, Michaelis, and Dathe contend, that instead of {tashoovoo,} "ye shall return," we should read {chashevoo,} "they designed."

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:13
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Therefore. Ge 32:13-20; 2Ch 32:2-8; Ps 112:5; Mt 10:16; 1Co 14:20 in the lower places. Heb. from the lower parts of the place,etc. their swords. 17,18; So 3:7,8; Eph 6:11-20

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:16
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
my servants. 23; 5:15,16; Ps 101:6 and the other half.This is no unusual thing in Palestine, even at the present day; people sowing their seed are often attended by armed men, to prevent the Arabs from robbing them of it.

habergeons.{Habergeon,} from the Teutonic {hals,} the neck, and {bergen,} to cover, defend, may be considered as signifying a breast-plate, though the Franco-Gallic {hautbergon} signifies a coat of mail; the original {shiryon,} we have already seen, denotes a corslet.

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:17
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
bare burdens. 10 every one.That is, he had his arms at hand; and was as fully prepared to fight as to work. The builders could not possibly have made any progress, if they had literally held a weapon in one of their hands; but the expression is evidently figurative, implying that every man was a much a soldier as a builder.

with one. Da 9:25; 1Co 9:12; 16:9,13; 2Co 6:7; Eph 6:11-20; Php 1:28; 2Ti 2:3 2Ti 4:7

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:18
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: by his side. Heb. on his loins. he that sounded. Nu 10:9; 2Ch 13:12-17

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:22
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: every one. 11:1,2

entries.title: Nehemiah 4:23
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: So neither I. 5:16; 7:2; Jud 9:48; 1Co 15:10 saving that, etc. or, every one went with his weapon forwater. Jud 5:11 The original of this obscure clause is {ish shilcho hammayim,} which is rendered by Montanus, {vir missile suum aquas,} "a man his dart to the waters," of which it is difficult to make sense. It is wholly omitted by the LXX.; and one of De Rossi's MSS. reads, {meshallachah �l hammayim,} "in order to send them to the water."
